description: WAVE A part 3 of 3 — move the BULK path fill server-side too ('bulk wala to aadha abhi render pe hai to pura wahi pe kar do'). Today bulk PDF CONVERSION already goes to Render (pdf_convert / pdf_convert_batch job kinds), but the FILLING still happens in the browser (Bulk Generate PDFs, Download Center, PDF Export, ReceiptModal all use docxFill.js). The user wants the bulk FILLING moved to Render as well so the whole bulk operation is server-side. Design: Render receives the TEMPLATE bytes + per-record fill DATA (not pre-filled docx), FILLS each record using FEAT-002's renderer, then converts to PDF, returning per-record PDF bytes; the Worker writes R2 + the generated_files index per record exactly as today. This extends the EXISTING pdf_convert / pdf_convert_batch plumbing (createAndDispatchJob storePayload rule, idempotent handleRenderCallback, applyPdfConvertResult/BatchResult, planBatches) rather than building new plumbing — the change is 'send data+template instead of filled bytes, and fill on arrival'. The per-result render report (missing tags/images) must travel with each record's result (FEAT-002 non-singleton design), surfaced to the bulk UI. Byte contract: filling on Render means the INPUT is now template-bytes-once + N small data payloads instead of N filled docx — re-evaluate the caps (this likely REDUCES input bytes since the template is sent once) and keep the drift test green.
steps: Prove-first: read and extend the existing bulk tests (mgmt/server-render/test/pdfConvert.test.mjs and the Worker's pdf_convert/batch coverage) to pin current bulk behaviour: per-record success/skip/failure shapes, the dedup skip (already-generated returns success:true skipped), the batch splitting via planBatches, and that the Worker writes R2 + index per record on the callback. Capture a golden for a bulk fill+convert of a couple of records using FEAT-002's fixtures.

Extend the job kinds so Render FILLS then converts. Two viable shapes — pick and justify: (A) reuse pdf_convert/pdf_convert_batch but change the payload from { base64: filledDocx } to { templateBase64, data, recordId, fileName } and have runPdfConvert/runPdfConvertBatch call the FEAT-002 renderer to fill BEFORE convertDocxToPdfBytes; or (B) add docx_render_batch as a distinct kind. Recommended (A)-with-versioned-payload or (B) as a clean new kind to avoid a mixed payload contract; whichever is chosen, the template is sent ONCE per batch (all records in a batch share docType+year+template) with per-record data, which reduces input bytes vs sending N filled docx. Register in HANDLERS + KINDS consistently with FEAT-003.

Template resolution mirrors FEAT-003: the Worker resolves the template via getDocxTemplate (Drive + KV cache) once per batch and sends the bytes in the dispatch; Render fills each record's data against it. Confirm the batch input (one template + N data blobs + N PDFs back) fits MAX_INPUT_TOTAL_BYTES(8MB) / MAX_OUTPUT_TOTAL_BYTES(6MB); adjust planBatches accounting so it sizes batches by template-once + data + expected output rather than by filled-docx-in bytes. If any cap needs changing, change renderContract.js + batchContract.js identically and keep render-batch-contract.test.mjs green.

Rewrite dispatchBulkPdfConvert / dispatchBulkPdfBatch in docxTemplates.js: keep the Worker-side dedup read (isFileGenerated), the Superadmin gate, assertRecordIdMatches, and the R2+index write on callback (applyPdfConvertResult / applyPdfConvertBatchResult) UNCHANGED in trust boundary; change only what is dispatched (template + data instead of filled bytes) and have the fill happen on Render. Preserve the synchronous in-Worker fallback semantics when Render is not configured — BUT note the Worker cannot fill+convert in-Worker without docxtemplater in the Worker (which the queue design deliberately avoided); decide the fallback: either keep a Worker-side fill fallback using the shared renderer if feasible within CPU limits, or make the no-Render case a clear error for bulk (justify — bulk is Superadmin and Render is expected to be configured for launch).

Carry the per-record render report (missingTags/missingImages from FEAT-002's per-call report) back through the callback into the per-record result the bulk UI reads, so a bulk run surfaces which records had unresolved placeholders (parity with the browser's getLastRenderReport warning today). Ensure base64 is STILL stripped from the stored D1 result (handleRenderCallback stripHeavyResult / normalizeBatchResult stay effective).

Update the bulk frontend surfaces (Bulk Generate PDFs, Download Center, PDF Export, ReceiptModal in mgmt/frontend, and the Svelte equivalents) to stop filling in the browser: they now send template-selection + record data (or just record refs, letting the Worker resolve the template) instead of filled base64. Confirm docxFill.js/qrCode.js can be removed from the bulk browser path. Re-check the mgmt/frontend 230kB main-chunk budget — with BOTH auto (FEAT-003) and bulk now server-side, docxtemplater/pizzip/image-module/qrcode should be droppable from the SPA entirely if nothing else uses them (grep for remaining imports); if fully removed, the main chunk should drop well below budget.

Confirm the renderer files docxFill.js (React) and docxFill.ts (Svelte) are now unused by production code and either delete them or leave with a deprecation note — decide based on remaining imports; if the guard test in FEAT-005 or any other code still references them, coordinate. The server-render renderer (FEAT-002) is now the single source of fill behaviour.

Mutation-test: break the per-record report propagation (drop the report) and confirm a test catches missing-tag surfacing; corrupt planBatches sizing to exceed a cap and confirm the contract/drift or a batch-size test fails; make the callback double-write the index for one record and confirm the idempotency/claim test fails.

Commit on a feature branch (e.g. wave-a3-bulk-serverside-fill). Do NOT push. Depends on FEAT-002 (renderer) and should follow FEAT-003 to reuse the docx_render fill primitive and any contract changes.
acceptance_criteria: Bulk generation (Bulk Generate PDFs, Download Center, PDF Export, ReceiptModal) no longer fills the .docx in the browser: Render fills each record from template+data then converts to PDF.

The existing bulk plumbing is reused (createAndDispatchJob storePayload, idempotent handleRenderCallback, applyPdfConvert*Result, planBatches) — no new callback/dispatch machinery; only the payload + fill step changed.
Template resolved Worker-side (Drive + KV cache) and sent once per batch; Render never touches D1/R2; Worker writes R2 + generated_files per record unchanged.
Per-record render report (missing tags/images) travels back to the bulk UI (parity with the browser warning today), using FEAT-002's per-call non-singleton report.
Byte contract still holds and render-batch-contract.test.mjs (drift) passes; planBatches sizes batches correctly for the template-once + data model.
mgmt/frontend main chunk stays under 230kB; docxtemplater/pizzip/qrcode removed from the SPA if no longer used (confirmed by grep).
cd mgmt/backend && npm test and cd mgmt/server-render && npm ci && npm test both pass.
Mutation checks recorded for report-drop, batch-size, and callback-double-write.
verification: cd mgmt/server-render && npm ci && npm test
cd mgmt/frontend && npm ci && npm run build (confirm main chunk < 230000 bytes; grep src for residual docxtemplater/qrcode imports)
